params.body:
The judge refuted two true claims against a measurement taken before the change had landed. elixir#199 stops that happening again; this is about the two verdicts already written, and about the general case.

A refutation is permanent in the rung (`10 confirmed, 0 refuted`), so one wrong one closes a door that does not reopen. But a ledger is not rewritten, so this is a **withdrawal, not a rewrite**:

- the verdict stays on the run as `wasVerdict`, with `wasEvidence` and `withdrawn: {reason, at}`
- `verdict` returns to `unjudged`, so the next reading decides it properly
- a reader sees what happened; the counting sees a run nobody has judged yet
- `elixir:ledger-withdraw <playbook> <url> --reason="…"`, a person's hand only, and refused without a reason

After merging, on the box:

```
php artisan elixir:ledger-withdraw headers https://github.com/abovebeyond-ai/abovebeyond/pull/134 --reason="judged against an exposure measurement from before the merge; the site was already sending all three headers"
php artisan elixir:ledger-withdraw headers https://github.com/ShaneDeconinck/good-governance/pull/24 --reason="judged against an exposure measurement from before the merge, and before the deploy"
```

Then the next exposure round judges both on what the sites actually answer.

650 tests, PHPStan, Pint.
params.title: A verdict that rested on the wrong evidence can be withdrawn, visibly
